title: Riverbend Council of Governments
text:
Riverbend Council of Governments
Stronger together. The Riverbend Council of Governments brings 24 boroughs, townships and cities in the Riverbend valley together to solve problems no town can solve alone: shared services, stormwater, public safety and grant funding.
Programs: Shared Fire Services, Stormwater Partnership, Digital Services Cohort.

title: About
text:
About
The Riverbend Council of Governments (RCOG) is a nonprofit membership organization of local governments. Members are municipalities. A municipality becomes a member when its council passes a resolution to join and pays annual dues based on its population. Members get research support, a seat at quarterly member meetings, and help applying for regional grants.
To ask about membership, email us (email: info@riverbend.example.org).

title: Shared Fire Services
text:
Shared Fire Services
STAGE OF ENGAGEMENT: IMPLEMENTING
Volunteer fire companies across the valley report fewer volunteers and slower daytime response. The Shared Fire Services program helps neighboring municipalities share duty crews, training and equipment, and studies regional fire service models. Five member municipalities joined the first cohort in 2025.
The program published the Volunteer Fire Staffing Study (https://riverbend.example.org/files/fire-staffing-study.pdf).
Get in touch with the Public Safety Director (email: safety@riverbend.example.org).

title: Stormwater Partnership
text:
Stormwater Partnership
STAGE OF ENGAGEMENT: EXPLORING
Heavy storms are flooding main streets more often. The Stormwater Partnership helps member municipalities plan green infrastructure together, compare stormwater fee programs, and apply jointly for state grants.
Get in touch with the Infrastructure Director (email: infrastructure@riverbend.example.org).

title: Digital Services Cohort
text:
Digital Services Cohort
STAGE OF ENGAGEMENT: EXPLORING
A peer group for small municipalities modernizing their websites, online permits and records. Members share templates and vendor reviews.
Get in touch (email: info@riverbend.example.org).

title: Volunteer Fire Staffing Study
pages: Volunteer Fire Staffing Study. Executive summary: active volunteer firefighters in the valley fell by a third between 2015 and 2025, and daytime calls are hardest to staff.
Findings: municipalities that share a paid daytime duty crew with a neighbor kept response times under ten minutes. Joint recruitment and shared training cut costs for small boroughs.
Recommendations: start with a shared daytime duty crew between two or three neighbors, standardize training, and plan a joint recruitment campaign. Talk to the Public Safety Director before starting.
